name: Beypore Fishing Harbour Seafood Stalls
signature_dish: Fresh-off-the-boat fish fry — the day's catch fried at waterfront stalls
why_it_matters: Beypore Fishing Harbour is one of the oldest ports in Kerala and a working fishing jetty — street vendors and small eateries line the waterfront frying the day's catch with traditional Kerala spices. With Beypore itself having almost no formal restaurants, the harbour stalls are the genuine on-site eating experience, alongside the famous dhow (uru) shipyards.
insider_tip: Come when the boats land (mid-morning and again late afternoon) for the freshest fish — you can buy a fish at the auction and have a nearby stall fry it. Cash only; this is informal harbour eating, not a sit-down restaurant. Pair with a walk past the uru shipyards.
signature_address: Beypore Fishing Harbour, Beypore, Kozhikode District, Kerala 673015

name: Paragon Restaurant
area: Kannur Road, Kozhikode — 10km north of Beypore
signature_dish: Kozhikode (Malabar) chicken dum biryani — the city's most iconic biryani
why_it_matters: Beypore has almost no formal restaurants of its own, so visitors eat in Kozhikode city 10km north. Paragon, founded 1939 on Kannur Road, is the single most cited Malabar biryani address — its biryani ranked on TasteAtlas's most-iconic-dishes list — and the obvious sit-down meal when visiting the Beypore port and shipyards.
insider_tip: A 10km drive north of Beypore into Kozhikode city. Go off-peak (3-4pm) to avoid the queue; order the fish pollichathu alongside the biryani. Combine a Beypore harbour visit with a Paragon lunch on the way in or out.
signature_address: Paragon Restaurant, Kannur Road, near CH Overbridge, Kozhikode, Kerala 673004

name: Bombay Hotel
area: Silk Street (SM Street), Kozhikode — 10km north of Beypore
signature_dish: Malabar evening snacks platter — chatti pathiri, unnakkaya, elanchi
why_it_matters: With Beypore lacking restaurants of its own, Bombay Hotel — opened 1949 on Silk Street in Kozhikode city, 10km north — is one of the area's oldest running eateries and the most-cited stop for Malabar teatime snacks. It pairs naturally with a Beypore harbour and uru-shipyard visit.
insider_tip: A 10km drive into Kozhikode city. Arrive by 4pm for the evening snack counter — chatti pathiri, unnakkaya, elanchi — which is what the hotel is famous for. Dum biryani is served noon to 3pm.
signature_address: Bombay Hotel, Silk Street, near Big Bazaar, Kozhikode, Kerala 673001

name: Hotel Sagar
area: Mavoor Road, Kozhikode — 11km north of Beypore
signature_dish: Ayila mulakittathu — mackerel in fiery red chilli gravy, with Malabar porotta
why_it_matters: Beypore has no formal restaurants of its own; Hotel Sagar on Mavoor Road in Kozhikode city, 11km north, is one of the city's oldest running eateries and the everyday Malabar-meals address — porottas, fish and meat curries — a practical, well-priced stop for Beypore visitors.
insider_tip: An 11km drive into Kozhikode city near the KSRTC bus stand. Order the ayila (mackerel) mulakittathu with porotta. Useful for travellers arriving in the city by bus before heading down to the Beypore port.
signature_address: Hotel Sagar, Mavoor Road, opposite Big Bazaar near KSRTC Bus Stand, Kozhikode, Kerala 673001

name: Indian Coffee House Mananchira
area: Mananchira Square, Kozhikode — 10km north of Beypore
signature_dish: Filter coffee with masala dosa — worker-cooperative cafe staples
why_it_matters: Beypore lacks cafes of its own, so the Indian Coffee House branch near Mananchira in Kozhikode city, 10km north, is the reliable budget breakfast and coffee stop — a worker-cooperative chain that is a genuine Kerala institution.
insider_tip: A 10km drive into Kozhikode city; best for an early, cheap breakfast before a day at the Beypore harbour and shipyards. Masala dosa and filter coffee; cooperative pricing.
signature_address: Indian Coffee House, Mavoor Road, near Mananchira, Kozhikode, Kerala 673001
